Morning on the second terrace. {#if query flag(:wren_joined)}Wren is asleep on the roof of the lamp store, one boot off, with her tally of the Dim on her arm in charcoal.{#else}Nobody has seen the courier since the road went quiet.{/if}
{#if query any_ruin()}There are ruins where there were lamps, and Ilse is already walking among them with her can.{#else}Every lamp is where it was left. That has not happened before.{/if}
{#if query any_injured()}The infirmary has a visitor's chair and a patient who will not stay in the bed.{/if}

Morning on the third. {#if query decided(:focus_fire)}Corvin has painted a mark on the wall for every husk his road took, and has run out of wall.{/if}{#if query decided(:lamps_work)}Ilse has hung a husk's shell over the lamp store as a sign.{/if}

{#if query decided(:cover_wren)}Wren has taken to walking half a step behind Corvin. He has stopped pretending not to notice.{/if}{#if query decided(:hold_the_line)}Wren does not meet your eye, and runs the messages faster than anyone needs.{/if}
The east road is open. Beyond the Mill, the fog has drawn back by a terrace overnight.

Morning on the last day. {#if query decided(:evacuate_mill)}The Mill is empty and the grain with it; the village has been eating thin soup and not complaining.{/if}{#if query decided(:call_militia)}The militia is on the Mill road with their forks, and they are proud and tired and a little drunk.{/if}

{#if query decided(:side_by_side)}Ilse and Corvin are sharing a table. They have not yet started to talk, but the table is shared.{/if}{#if query decided(:give_minute)}Ilse's east lamp is the brightest on the hill and she has told everyone.{/if}{#if query decided(:no_time)}The east lamp is dark. Ilse has not mentioned it, and that is how you know.{/if}
The fog has thinned to a rope below the last terrace. Something in it is looking up.
The Lantern keeps. By midmorning the fog has gone back below the last terrace, and the village is up on its roofs, mending, and shouting at each other about nothing.

{#if query dead(:ilse)}Ilse's place at the table is hers.{#else}{#if query trust_high(:ilse)}Ilse has the lamps trimmed before dawn and never once asks you to hurry.{#else}{#if query trust_mid(:ilse)}Ilse nods at the lamps. "They will hold. Mostly."{#else}Ilse keeps her tools in her apron and her opinions to herself.{/if}{/if}{/if}

{#if query dead(:corvin)}Corvin's road is still on the map in his hand.{#else}{#if query trust_high(:corvin)}Corvin walks the road with you to the gate, the way a captain walks with his own.{#else}{#if query trust_mid(:corvin)}Corvin salutes, short and dry. It is the most he gives anyone.{#else}Corvin says the road was his, and goes home without waiting for you.{/if}{/if}{/if}

{#if query dead(:wren)}Somebody else carries the messages now.{#else}{#if query trust_high(:wren)}Wren has already named the next dawn's first runner after herself.{#else}{#if query trust_mid(:wren)}Wren waves from the switchbacks and shouts the news before anyone asks.{#else}Wren keeps her distance, though she still runs the messages.{/if}{/if}{/if}
The Lantern keeps, at a cost. The terraces are burned and broken, and the fog is only fog now, but the places at the table are not all filled.

{#if query dead(:ilse)}Somebody has hung Ilse's can of oil over the lamp store door.{/if}{#if query dead(:corvin)}The road is Corvin's. They have named it.{/if}{#if query dead(:wren)}Nobody runs the messages on the switchbacks any more. It is very quiet.{/if}{#if query bell_ruined()}The Bellfrey's bell is a piece of the museum already.{/if}
You stand on the wall and the village stands with you. It is not quite nothing.

You sounded the retreat, and they carried the flame down the hill in a lantern. The Lantern stands empty at the top of Marrow Hill. For the first time in a hundred years, there is nothing on the terraces to defend.
Ilse carries the oil and Corvin carries the road. Wren runs ahead, as ever, and does not look back.
The Lantern goes out. In the fog, something notices, and begins at last to climb.
Marrow Hill is dark. In the morning the village is not there, and the fog is a little thicker, and more patient.
Watch the road. Not the lamps. The road.
They are on the second switchback! I counted. Thirty, maybe more, and they are not even hurrying.
You are the courier. Courier, you are in the wrong place.
I am in the only place I can see them from.
Corvin looks at you. It is your terrace, and your call.
Stay behind the lamps, then. Warden, give her something to do.
Those are shells, not bodies. The lamps will burn through them if we give them time.
We have no time. Hit them where they stop, all lamps at once, and the road holds.
Good. Every lamp on one husk, then the next. Ilse, you will have your oil's worth.
I will have a long night of mending, is what I will have.
Thank you. Steady, now. A lamp that is allowed to finish is worth three that are rushed.
If the road breaks, it breaks on your say.
I cannot get back! They are between me and the lamps!
Warden. She is not a lamp and she is not a wall. Say the word.
Moving. If the road breaks I will remember whose idea this was.
I will remember it better.
Hold! Wren, run for the lamps. Run as if the hill were on fire.
You are the Warden, and you decided that. I heard you.
The east road and the switchbacks meet at one terrace, and two stubborn people have found themselves standing on it.
Left lamp. Now the right. Ilse, the oil.
I know where the oil is, Captain. Hold the gap and I will keep your lamps burning.
For one quiet minute they do not argue. Then the husks come, and nobody has time to.
That was not so bad.
It was tolerable.
The Dim have reached the Mill road, and the Mill is full of people who thought it was the safe place.
Militia can hold the lane for a quarter of an hour. Or you empty the Mill and let the Dim have the empty building.
Pitchforks to the lane. Nobody is a hero tonight; everybody is a wall.
Out. Out, and uphill. We keep the people and lose the grain.
The east light is guttering. If I do not trim it now it goes out in the middle of the rush. A minute, Warden. One.
Thank you. There. Now every lamp near me is mended, and I am not sorry.
Then it goes out. I will remember that you chose the rush over the lamp.
The fog below the last terrace parts like a curtain. Something the size of a barn climbs out of it, slowly, and the lamps nearest it begin to burn the wrong colour.
That is not one of them. That is where they come from.
Then we do not let it reach the Lantern. Everything on it.
One of them is down on the road, and the Dim are closing around the place.
Someone goes. Someone always does. The line behind them thins.
You choose the line. Nobody says anything afterwards. That is what it costs.
The Bellfrey has rung every night since the Lantern was lit. It stops. The silence is louder than the bell was.
I can burn the approach. A flare big enough to show them all, and burn them while they look. Or we fall back to the Lantern and make a stand there.
Look, then. Look at all of it.
To me. The Lantern, and nothing else, until it is done.
Twelve have passed the last lamp. The Lantern flickers, and the heat of it is leaving the terrace.
We can still carry it down. The flame, I mean. Out of the hill. It would live.
Carry it down. Carry it slowly. Do not look back at the hill.
Then we stand. Every one of us. Hear me, Warden: you asked that.
The Maw folds, and the valley is empty of everything but fog. The fog, for the first time in anyone's memory, is only fog.
The line breaks. Below, the Lantern gutters, and the valley goes dark.
Marrow Hill is built in terraces on a steep hillside, and every terrace is lit. Below the last of them the valley is a lake of fog, and nothing in the fog has ever been seen to stop moving.
You arrive with an old key and a letter. The letter says that the last Warden is gone, and that a lantern burns brightest for people who are trusted.
You are the Warden? I was told to expect a person, not a coat on a stick. I am Ilse. I trim the lamps and I mend what breaks.
Captain Corvin, retired. I know the roads. Whether you will let me tell you about them is the question.
Ilse sets down her can of oil. Corvin does not sit down at all.
Dusk is the hour. The Dim climbs the switchbacks towards the Lantern, and the Lantern burns only while somebody is minding it.
Build where the road turns. A lamp that cannot see the road is a candle.
Far below, the fog moves. It is not wind.
